pr.title: Keep one review worktree per pull request, and prune the rest
pr.head: fa9186c021a8e4abbc046a468b943194d789c905

summary: A Projector review runs in a scratch worktree: a full Git checkout of the head under review that project review setup creates under the review state directory, ~/.local/state/projector/reviews/worktrees/<owner>/<repo>/<pr>/<model-key>/<short-sha>. Before this change, only project review finish, run when the pull request closes, removed those checkouts. A review loop creates one for every head it reviews, so a long-lived pull request kept dozens of them. On a large monorepo, where reviewers also install dependencies in each checkout, that filled a 500 GB disk.
This pull request makes each review keep one checkout at a time, and adds a command that sweeps what is left over:

• Setup and move remove the earlier heads' worktrees. Once the new head's worktree exists, setup and move remove the worktrees that the model's state lists for earlier heads. A worktree whose head lock is held and less than a day old stays, because a review may still be reading it.
  • project review prune sweeps the rest. It lists every worktree under the state directory that no review needs, and removes them only with --apply. That covers earlier heads' worktrees, folders from the older layout with no model folder, worktrees under a model with no review set up, and the current worktree of a closed pull request.

At this head, prune reads each worktree's head lock and review state again just before removing it, so a setup or move that starts while prune waits on GitHub keeps its worktree. The Codex rules shown in docs/cli.md now list prune, and a test compares that block with the rules project init writes. The automated review has one open finding: two edited lines in docs/cli.md break the file's 80-column wrapping. The change does not touch the fetch in setup, so the separately reported FETCH_HEAD race is out of scope.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Scratch worktree: the checkout of one head that a review reads and runs tests in.
  • Model key: the folder name made from a model ID, so each model reviewing a pull request keeps its own state and worktrees.
  • Head lock: the file prs/<owner>/<repo>/<pr>/<model-key>/<sha>.lock that a review holds from setup until publish. A lock older than a day is stale.
  • State: state.json beside the locks, which names the review's current worktree.

cards.title: What prune keeps
cards.html:
WorktreePrune
Head lock held, under a day oldKeeps
A review's current head, pull request openKeeps
A review's current head, GitHub cannot sayKeeps
A review's current head, pull request closedRemoves
Any other head under a model with a reviewRemoves
Under a model with no review set upRemoves
<pr>/<short-sha>, the older layoutRemoves

groups.title: One worktree per review, and a sweep for the rest
groups.kicker: The review module removes superseded worktrees on setup and move, and adds prune.
intro: Each review's state lists the worktrees it made, under worktrees, and names the current one under worktree. remove_superseded now runs at the end of setup and move. It removes every listed worktree except the new head's, unless that head's lock is held, and keeps one whose removal fails so that finish can try again. It never fails the command that called it, because that command has already posted or edited its start comment.

prune works from the state directory alone. It reads every head lock and every review state, asks GitHub whether each reviewed pull request is open, and then walks the worktree folders, as the table in the overview describes. To remove a worktree, it runs git worktree remove in the repository named by the worktree's .git file. When that fails, or the checkout is gone, it deletes the folder directly, and it unlinks a symbolic link without following it. Just before each removal, needed_now reads that worktree's head lock and review state again, and keeps the worktree when a review set up since the first read needs it.

checks.text: A head lock is the only signal that a review is in progress before its state is written. setup takes the lock first, then fetches, creates the worktree, posts the start comment, and writes the state last.

files.note: Adds remove_superseded, used by setup and move, and the prune sweep with its helpers, including the per-worktree re-check in needed_now.

checks.text: A setup that starts while prune waits on GitHub keeps its worktree. needed_now re-reads the head lock and state just before each removal. Checked with a test that runs a real setup of a new head inside prune's pull request lookup: prune --apply keeps the new worktree because its lock is held. test_a_review_set_up_while_prune_asks_github_keeps_its_worktree also covers a review published meanwhile.

An older-layout <pr>/<short-sha> folder holds a .git file, so prune treats it as one worktree rather than as a model folder. The current release reads no state from that layout, so no live review owns one. Checked by reading and by test_lists_leftovers_without_apply_and_removes_them_with_it.

remove_superseded only touches worktrees listed in this model's own state, so another model's review keeps its worktree. Checked by reading and by test_another_models_worktree_stays, which passes at this head.

files.note: Adds the review prune subcommand with --repo, --state-dir, --apply, and --json, and prints each worktree that setup or move removed.

checks.text: prune runs before the loop and model are read, so it takes no --loop or --model. It exits 1 when any removal fails.

files.note: Adds SupersededWorktreeTests and PruneTests, which run real Git against a fake GitHub, and updates a finish test to the new count of listed worktrees.

groups.title: Letting Codex run prune
groups.kicker: The Codex rules that project init writes now allow review prune.
intro: project init writes a Codex rules file that allows Projector's review steps by name. This change adds prune to that list, beside finish and the other steps that only touch Projector's own state.

files.note: Adds prune to the allowed project review subcommands.

checks.text: The rules block in docs/cli.md now lists prune, and test_the_documented_codex_rules_are_the_ones_init_writes compares every documented pattern with CODEX_ALLOW. It passes at this head.

files.note: Expects prune in the allowed list, and checks that the rules documented in docs/cli.md match CODEX_ALLOW.

groups.title: Documentation and skills
groups.kicker: The CLI reference describes prune, and the loop skills say each head's setup cleans up.
intro: The CLI reference documents what setup, move, and finish now remove, and adds a section on prune with a table of what it removes. The review-pr and start-review-loop skills tell a loop subagent to keep its review set up between heads, since the next head's setup removes the earlier checkout.

files.note: Documents the cleanup in setup, move, and finish, and adds the prune section.
